warnings.headline: Storm Boelo will bring a very windy and wet spell this weekend with some disruption likely across parts of northern UK. : UPDATED
warnings.description:
Information on update: Warning extended further south across northern England and into north Wales. . Strong winds will spread across northern parts of the UK during Saturday afternoon, combining with spells of heavy rain. Initially strong southerly winds will affect parts of Scotland before more widespread and even stronger westerly winds develop later on Saturday. Very windy conditions will then persist overnight and through much of Sunday before gradually easing from the southwest later. Gusts of 55-65 mph are likely widely with some coastal and exposed areas potentially seeing gusts of 70-80 mph or more, these strongest gusts most likely across Scotland and the far north of England.

warnings.headline: Heavy rain brings a high likelihood of moderate impacts from surface water flooding.
warnings.description:
Heavy rain in association with Storm Boelo is expected to lead to surface water flooding in places. 25-30mm is expected widely across the warning area during this time, with a few places such as upland areas seeing 50-60mm, and some of this perhaps falling within 6 hours. Rain will ease for a time through the evening, but this will be followed by another intense band of heavy rain following in from the west, before the whole system clears away eastward to bring a clear night with a few scattered showers following on.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings

warnings.headline: A period of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.
warnings.description:
Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland, the north of Northern Ireland and northern England on Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas could see gusts of 70 mph or more, but at this time there is some uncertainty in where, and how strong, the peak gusts will be. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.



For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Irish Sea at New Brighton
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding this evening. 

Flooding is expected from 10:45 PM 24 October 2026. 

Locations most affected will be Marine Point Leisure and Retail Park. We anticipate the next high tide tomorrow afternoon, 25 October 2026, to meet the flood alert threshold. We are expecting higher than normal high tides over the next 2 days, and a result, we may issue further flood alerts and flood warnings. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Start acting on your flood plan if you have one.   

This message will be updated by 9:30AM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
warnings.instruction:
Act now 
 
You should: 
- go to Check for flooding for a map of the area and to monitor up-to-date local flood information – https://check-for-flooding.service.gov.uk/target-area/013FWTTME12  
- act on your personal flood plan if you have one - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/personal-flood-plan 
- follow the guidance in 'What to do before or during a flood' - https://www.gov.uk/help-du

warnings.event: Flood Warning: River Barle from Simonsbath to Brushford, including Withypool
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: River Barle from Simonsbath to Brushford, including Withypool
warnings.description:
High river levels are expected to cause flooding today. 

Flooding is expected on Saturday 24 October  

Properties and low lying areas will start to flood from around 7 pm on Saturday. The main areas of concern are Simonsbath and Brushford, including Simonsbath, Withypool, Newbridge, Northmoor Road, Brushford and the B3222 and B3223 at Dulverton. Flood waters may be deep and fast flowing in these areas. 
River levels are forecast to be at their highest between 6 pm and 10 pm. 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.   

This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
